packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-19 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
No proposed identification of work or author was present in my context. I read
PROMPT.md and the image files only. I listed the packet directory (file names
and sizes) to find the images; packet.json was not opened. No web or search
tool was used.

RUNNING NOTES PER IMAGE (written as viewed)

image-001.jpg (reduced overview): spine of a small book, lying horizontally,
with a colour/scale target below it (target printed "chsopensource.org",
upside down, mm scale). The spine covering is darkened, glossy, yellow-brown
parchment carrying writing: one line of large black formal gothic script
(textualis) runs along the length of the spine near its lower edge, with
traces of a second line above it (tops/bottoms of letters near the upper
right). The text is upright in this frame (reads left to right). Raised bands
or cords cross the spine at about one quarter and one half of its length.
Overview-level reading of the lower line, very uncertain:
  [...]?dom[...] [illegible] [...]?ensione?[...] [illegible] ?mandadit? [...] ?ordinum?
(these are shapes seen at reduced size; see tiles below for corrections).

image-002.jpg (native tile, right end of spine):
line 1 (upper line, only bottoms of letters / fragments): [...] ?ill [...] (three or
        four minims with a taller stroke; nothing connected)
line 2 (lower line): [...]?dn(?)t(?) [..] ?ordin(um?)  -- at left "ndsit"/"ndrit"-like
        group ("-ndrit"? "-ndat"?), then a gap at a crease, then a word
        beginning with a tall letter (possibly "p" or long "s"/"f" + "o") and
        reading "?ordinu(m)" / "?ordmun" - a "d" with rounded back is clear,
        followed by a run of minims. Right end abraded.

image-003.jpg (native tile, spine right of centre; overlaps image-002 at its
right edge - the group ending "-dr.." at the right margin here is the same
group as the left of image-002 line 2; also shows the scale target):
line 1 (lower line of script; only one line legible in this tile):
        [...]?ione [gap of c. 6-8 letters, surface glossy and abraded]
        ?mandaud?r[...]
  Notes: at far left, before the raised band, the end of a word "-one" or
  "-ione"/"-ons" (round letters, o and e fairly clear). After the gap: an
  enlarged or at least taller first letter (two uprights with a top bar -
  "M"/"N"/"U"?), then minims, a clear round-backed "d", "a", "u" or "n", "d",
  then a letter with a low stroke ("r"/"i"), running off the tile: read as
  ?mandaud..., ?uiridaud..., or ?nu(n)c daud... - not resolved. No upper line
  legible here (surface glare).

image-004.jpg (native tile, left end of spine; overlap with image-003 at its
right edge is in the abraded zone, no legible repeated text):
line 1 (lower line of script):
        [...] ?ar(?)dtioni  ?me(?) [..] ?co(n)[illegible]
  Notes: left end of the line is lost in abrasion (2-4 letters). Then a word
  whose legible part is a round letter, "r"?, round-backed "d" or "a", "t",
  "i", "o", "n", and a final minim/"i" or "e": "-ationi"/"-ratione"/"-rdtioni"
  (?). Immediately after it the raised band; then short group "me"/"ine"/"nic"
  (?), then, after glare, traces "con"/"eon" (?) and further minims running
  into the zone that image-003 shows as "-ione".
  No upper line legible; some dark traces above the band at left may be
  offset or remains of a higher line.

image-005.jpg (reduced overview, second face): one board of the same binding,
seen flat, spine edge at left, with colour/scale target below. The covering is
a parchment leaf, heavily abraded, stained dark in large patches, with pale
losses of surface. The script on it runs at 90 degrees to the frame: lines of
writing appear as vertical bands running top to bottom of the cover, most
visibly in the upper left quarter and down the left third. Along the spine
edge (far left) one band of large black script is comparatively well
preserved; it is the continuation of the line seen on the spine in images
001-004 as it wraps over the joint. Two fastening/tie points (small
rectangular lacing slots or stubs) sit on the spine edge at about 1/6 and 2/3
of the height. No rubrics, initials, running titles, columns, or glosses can be
made out at overview scale. Vertical ruled-looking lines are visible between
the bands of script (line ruling of the reused leaf, tentative).

image-006.jpg (native tile, upper left of the cover, including the spine
edge and both of the upper fastening points):
Orientation: script is rotated; lines run vertically in the frame. I count
traces of about 7-8 lines (vertical bands) across the tile, from the spine
edge rightward. Letter forms are large formal gothic script (textualis) of the same size as
on the spine. Ink is almost entirely abraded on the board face; what survives
is mostly the brown ghost of minims.
- Band 1 (on the joint/spine edge, far left; best preserved): a continuous
  run of minims and round letters is visible from the top of the tile to the
  bottom; individual letters seen (reading with the frame rotated so the line
  is horizontal): groups of minims, a round-backed "d", "o", "p"-like descender
  forms. I could not obtain a single secure word from this tile at this angle:
  [illegible - c. 25-30 letters visible as shapes].
- Bands 2-4 (upper left of board): ghost minims only, in three parallel bands
  between y=250 and y=780 of the tile; [illegible].
- Bands 5-8: dark staining and scratches; [illegible].

image-007.jpg (native tile, upper right of the cover; overlaps image-006 on
its left edge - the dark horizontal stain and the pale loss are the same):
No readable script. Surface is abraded to a mottled grey-brown with a broad
dark horizontal stain across the middle and pale losses at lower right.
Faint vertical bands of ghost minims are just visible at upper left (around
x=150-400, y=250-580) - the same bands 5-8 noted in image-006 - and some later
scratched/pen-trial hatching at lower left (x=100-280, y=1560-1680). Neither
yields letters. [illegible throughout]

image-008.jpg (native tile, lower left of the cover, with the spine edge, the
lower fastening point, and the bottom corner; overlaps image-006 at its top
edge - the fastening point at top left here is the lower one of image-006):
- Band 1 on the joint/spine edge (far left): the large script continues the
  whole height of the tile down to c. y=1250 as a dense run of minims; letters
  are seen edge-on because the parchment turns over the joint. Shapes only:
  [illegible - c. 30 letters]. This is the same line read from the spine side
  in images 002-004 (probably the upper, fragmentary line there, or the next
  line of the leaf - not determinable).
- Board face: no script recoverable; dark blotches, pale losses, scratches.
  At upper right (x=1050-1200, y=280-470) and top right corner (x=1250-1460,
  y=100-230) there are later pen scribbles/hatching and a roughly circular
  doodle, not text. A few ghost minim bands at x=420-520, y=1060-1110 (short
  horizontal ladder-like strokes, i.e. minims of a vertical line): [illegible].

image-009.jpg (native tile, lower right of the first cover; overlaps image-007
at top and image-008 at left - the pen hatching at top left is the same as in
those tiles):
No readable script. Ghost minim bands (short horizontal ladder-like strokes
= minims of lines running vertically) at x=390-440, y=450-900; x=800-880,
y=540-680; x=640-700, y=740-900. One small isolated mark at x=650, y=570
resembles a "u"/cup shape (possibly a later pen mark). No letter can be
named with any confidence. [illegible throughout]

image-010.jpg (reduced overview, third face): the other board of the binding,
spine edge now at RIGHT (three fastening/tie points visible on the right
edge), fore-edge at left with a darker vertical strip (turn-in or a separate
strip of covering). Same parchment covering, even more abraded: pale
grey-brown, stains, scratches, a diagonal crease/tear at lower left. Ghost
bands of minims, again running vertically in the frame (script at 90 degrees),
are faintly visible at left centre (around x=510-580, y=300-400 of the
overview) and upper centre. No rubric, initial, or layout feature
distinguishable at this scale.

image-011.jpg (tile, upper half of the third face; spine edge at right with
two fastening points; this tile was shown to me downscaled from its native
size, so fine detail may be lost):
No readable script. Ghost minim bands (minims of lines running vertically in
the frame) at about x=340-400, y=560-680; x=660-720, y=700-770; x=1360-1400,
y=460-500; and a longer band down the right side near the spine edge at
x=1740-1790, y=540-800. Scratches at upper right are later damage. A brown
tide-line stain and two round stains at upper left. [illegible throughout]

image-012.jpg (tile, lower half of the third face; overlaps image-011 at its
top edge; also shown downscaled):
No readable script. Faint vertical lines (ruling or scratches) at x=1100-1140
and x=1380-1500 running most of the height; ghost traces of minims near
x=1280-1330, y=540-640. Diagonal crease/tear at lower left corner. One
fastening point on the spine edge at right (y=670). [illegible throughout]

======================================================================
CONSOLIDATED RESPONSE

LAYOUT SURVEY
Three faces of one small binding are shown: spine (image-001, tiles 002-004),
one board with the spine edge at left (image-005, tiles 006-009), the other
board with the spine edge at right (image-010, tiles 011-012). The whole
binding is covered in a reused parchment leaf written in a large formal
gothic script (textualis). Observation: on the spine the writing is upright and runs along
the length of the spine; on the boards the same orientation means the lines
run vertically in the frame (the leaf was wrapped with its lines parallel to
the spine). Line ruling is faintly visible between lines. I see no columns
division, running title, rubric, coloured initial, underlining, gloss, or
music anywhere; given the abrasion, their absence is not evidence that the
leaf had none. Tentative interpretation only: a single leaf (or bifolium) of
a large-format book reused as a limp/wrapper covering. No inference about
work, date, or origin is made.

SELECTED SPANS AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
Only the spine carries ink dark enough to read at all, and only its lower
line. I selected that line (images 004 -> 003 -> 002, left to right). All of
both boards remains unread: the ink there survives only as brown ghosts of
minims, with no letter I can name.

TRANSCRIPTION (spine, one physical line, split by tile; left to right)
image-004.jpg line 1:  [...] ?ar(?)dtioni  ?me(?) [..] ?co(n)[illegible]
image-003.jpg line 1:  [...]?ione [illegible, c. 6-8 letters] ?mandaud?r[...]
image-002.jpg line 2:  [...]?nd?rit(?) [..] ?ordinu(m?)[...]
image-002.jpg line 1 (line above, fragments only):  [...] ?ill [...]
Overlaps: the right end of image-003 line 1 and the left end of image-002
line 2 are the same letters (a group with round-backed "d" followed by "r"
or "i" and "t"); they are not additional text. The right end of image-004
and left end of image-003 meet in the "-ione" zone.

Joined, very tentatively, the line reads something like:
  [...]?-ationi ?me [...] ?con[...]?ione [...] ?mandaud?rit [...] ?ordinum [...]
Every word here carries a question mark. The most secure elements are single
letter forms: round-backed "d" (several), "o", "t-i-o-n" in the first word,
and the "-ord-" sequence followed by minims in the last word. I have not
supplied anything from sense.

LIMITATIONS
- The spine parchment is darkened, glossy, cockled over the sewing supports,
  and photographed with specular glare; roughly half of the single legible
  line is lost, and the letters that remain are partly seen obliquely.
- The line above it on the spine survives only as letter feet.
- Both boards are abraded beyond reading in visible light at this resolution.
  Tiles 011 and 012 reached me downscaled (about 0.72x), the others at native
  size.
- No span of ten or more connected lines exists in these images; the result
  is one broken line. This is too little for a checkable source match.
- Suggested for a better reading: raking-light, UV, or multispectral images of
  the spine and of the board edge next to the spine (band 1 in images 006 and
  008), and images of the inside of the covers / turn-ins, where the hair or
  flesh side protected from wear may keep its ink.
- This is an unverified image reading.
